clue.text: Big old plate for a warhorse

definitions.meaning: a large flat dish for serving meat, an old-fashioned word
a horse ridden into battle by a knight or cavalry officer

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a large antique serving platter and a cavalry mount trained for battle.

clue.text: I let Carole coach group to make pastry

indicators.note: to group is to arrange, so the letters of I let Carole coach are rearranged

explanation.surface: A coach party of friends gathered to bake a cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'group' is a verb meaning arrange, rearranging all fifteen letters of I LET CAROLE COACH.
explanation.definitionFit: An éclair filled with cream and topped with cocoa icing is a type of choux pastry.

clue.text: Sea-legs wobbly, unaffected by time

indicators.note: wobbly letters are unsteady, so the letters of sea-legs are mixed up

explanation.surface: A sailor's balance stays shaky however long they spend at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that never grows old or shows signs of years passing seems timeless.

clue.text: Partisan who goes in for a lot of breast-beating, we hear

indicators.note: signals that the word is heard rather than read

parts.words: who goes in for a lot of breast-beating
parts.note: the great ape famous for drumming on its chest

explanation.surface: A political zealot noted for beating their breast.
explanation.walkthrough: The great ape and the irregular fighter are pronounced alike.
explanation.definitionFit: An irregular fighter in a resistance band is a partisan.

clue.text: Overoptimistic, got up stirring tea

parts.note: rose means got up out of bed

indicators.note: stirring the letters of tea mixes them up

explanation.surface: Someone got out of bed and stirred their tea, feeling hopeful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stirring' looks like it describes the tea being made, but it only signals the shuffle of those three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Seeing things through rose-tinted glasses means being too optimistic.

clue.text: The French circle in test of bony fish

indicators.note: the words before it go inside the word test

parts.note: taken as written
le is French for 'the'
a circle is shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A French lesson, with a circle drawn into a test paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' marks the container: the French article and the circle go inside the word test, which the surface presents as an exam.
explanation.definitionFit: Zoologists use the term for the large group of ray-finned fishes with true bony skeletons.

clue.text: Trains knock the bottom off earl grey's carrier

indicators.note: in a down clue the bottom of the word is its last letter, which is removed

parts.note: a big box used to ship loose tea, Earl Grey being a tea blend

explanation.surface: A railway porter knocks the bottom out of a box of Earl Grey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knock the bottom off' removes the last letter T from TEA CHEST; Earl Grey is a bergamot-scented tea.
explanation.definitionFit: To train someone is to instruct them in a skill.

clue.text: Coming out of terrible hardship, his widow was merry

indicators.note: the letters come straight out of the run terrible hardship

explanation.surface: A widow emerged from terrible hardship in good spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across terribLE HARdship. The definition alludes to the operetta The Merry Widow.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Lehár composed the operetta The Merry Widow, so his widow was merry.

clue.text: Rough idea of unfashionable stock

parts.note: out means no longer in fashion
a line is a range of goods a shop stocks

explanation.surface: A vague impression of shop goods that have gone out of style.
explanation.definitionFit: A general sketch without detail gives the main points of a plan.

clue.text: New motoring article describing some angular functions

indicators.note: new letters means the letters of motoring and article are made into something fresh

explanation.surface: A new motoring magazine piece describing the car's angles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges the fifteen letters of MOTORING and ARTICLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Sine, cosine and tangent are functions of angles studied in that branch of mathematics.

clue.text: Neat look of a daisy

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, so one beast is an ox
to eye something is to look at it

explanation.surface: Someone admires the tidy look of a daisy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' reads as tidy, but here it is the old word for cattle, as in neatsfoot oil.
explanation.definitionFit: A common wild flower of meadows, white-petalled with a yellow centre, is a kind of daisy.

clue.text: Course of a motorway interchange

definitions.meaning: a course of a meal, here a pasta dish
... Junction is the nickname of a tangled motorway interchange near Birmingham, England

explanation.definitionFit: Long thin pasta is served as a course, and a knotted junction of looping roads is likened to a plateful of it.

clue.text: To get the better of bowling, stretch!

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled from one end
to reach is to stretch out an arm

explanation.surface: A cricket coach urges a fielder to stretch for the ball.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, the bowling comes in overs of six balls.
explanation.definitionFit: To outwit someone by cunning is an old sense of the verb, alongside straining too far.

clue.text: Old money one still charges in Africa

definitions.meaning: a horned beast of the savanna that still charges at intruders

explanation.definitionFit: The word is old British slang for cash and also the horned African animal famous for charging.

clue.text: Pardon sailor for crack

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a rank of sailor
to crack a puzzle is to solve it

explanation.surface: A seaman is forgiven for breaking something.
explanation.definitionFit: To forgive someone formally, as a priest does, clears them of guilt.

clue.text: Commander earlier into wrestling

indicators.note: the word for earlier goes inside the wrestling word

parts.note: sumo is Japanese wrestling
pre- is a prefix meaning before or earlier

explanation.surface: A military leader who once went in for wrestling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' marks the container; 'earlier' gives the familiar prefix meaning before.
explanation.definitionFit: A boss or overall leader with full authority is a top commander.

clue.text: Making progress unhurriedly — like Harry?

definitions.meaning: behaving like the boy wizard Harry, surname Potter

explanation.definitionFit: Ambling about at a leisurely pace is the plain sense; the whimsical second reading turns the wizard's surname into a verb.

clue.text: Passage to copy out

definitions.meaning: a short section quoted from a book or piece of music
to take out a piece of text for quoting

explanation.definitionFit: A quoted excerpt from a text is the noun, and to take such a piece out of a text is the verb.

clue.text: Belch-producing drinking-vessel?

parts.note: a jug shaped like a stout drinker, and Sir Toby Belch is the reveller in Shakespeare's Twelfth Night

explanation.definitionFit: The pottery mug moulded as a jolly seated man shares its first name with Shakespeare's Sir Toby Belch.

clue.text: Alarm signals said to be things dangerous to our systems

indicators.note: signals that the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: toxins are poisons harmful to the body's systems

explanation.surface: Warnings raised about substances that harm the body.
explanation.definitionFit: Bells rung to raise the alarm are old warning signals.

clue.text: Stuff for tea, as it turns out

indicators.note: the letters of tea, as it are turned out into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Food for afternoon tea, as it happens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns out' shuffles TEA and ASIT. 'Stuff' is a verb here: to fill completely.
explanation.definitionFit: To stuff someone with food is to fill them until they want no more.

clue.text: Northern eagles circling African republic

indicators.note: circling letters go round and round, so N and eagles are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Birds of prey wheel above a country in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circling' mixes N and EAGLES together into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: A West African country with its capital at Dakar is a republic.

clue.text: Sounds like there is a deliberate fire when in charge of poison

indicators.note: signals that the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: arson is a fire started on purpose

explanation.surface: An arsonist in charge is accused of a poisoning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sounds like' covers only the deliberate fire, said aloud and spelt as the start of the poison; 'when' and 'there is' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A grey metalloid element whose compounds are notoriously toxic.

clue.text: Once a measure of copper piece

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a bit is a small piece

explanation.surface: A small amount of copper was once used as a measure.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancient unit of length, roughly the forearm from elbow to fingertip, now obsolete.

clue.text: Slender key was yours once

parts.note: thin means slender
E is a musical key

explanation.surface: A thin key used to belong to you.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic possessive pronoun, as in old prayers, meant belonging to you.

clue.text: This capacitor contracts

parts.note: an older name for an electrical capacitor, also read as something that makes things smaller or denser

explanation.definitionFit: The device storing electric charge was formerly called by a name that also means a thing that compresses or concentrates.

clue.text: A daughter getting married next door

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter in family trees
joining is uniting in marriage

explanation.surface: A daughter is getting married to the boy next door.
explanation.definitionFit: Neighbouring rooms or houses share a wall, so one is beside the other.

clue.text: One advanced, in charge of architectural style

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
moved on means advanced

explanation.surface: A single leader moved forward to take charge of a building's design.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the classical orders of Greek column design, marked by scroll-shaped capitals.

clue.text: Men fitting out ships, hard ships some say

indicators.note: signals that the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: rigours are hardships, split here into two words

explanation.surface: Shipyard workers kitting out vessels that are tough to work on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hard ships' is really hardships, RIGOURS, which said in a non-rhotic accent matches the answer's sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Workers who set up the masts, ropes and tackle of a vessel do that trade.

clue.text: Find soldiers in pub? That's reasonable

indicators.note: the soldiers go inside the word for a pub

parts.note: a local is your nearest pub, in British usage
GIs are American soldiers

explanation.surface: Looking for troops in the pub makes sense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' marks the container. A 'local' is everyday British English for the pub nearest home.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sensible and well argued follows clear rules of reasoning.
